question.:question/problem:
Express $\sin(x-315^\circ)$ using $\sin x$ and $\cos x$. Enter exact coefficients, including their signs.

$\sin(x-315^\circ)=$ {{field-1}} $\sin x+$ {{field-2}} $\cos x$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the difference formula for sine:
$$
\sin(u-v)=\sin u\cos v-\cos u\sin v.
$$
Apply it and substitute the exact special-angle values:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x-315^\circ)&=\sin x\cos 315^\circ-\cos x\sin 315^\circ\\
&=\sin x\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\cos x\cdot\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$
The plus sign outside the second blank is supplied. The entries are $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, respectively.
